title: Design: Bundle-based spine architecture
description:
Background: Rheo's spine system (crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs) currently works by: (1) reading each vertebra .typ file, (2) transforming links via LinkTransformer, (3) concatenating sources for merged PDF or keeping them separate for HTML/EPUB. This is brittle manual glue that should be replaced by typst's native bundle format.

Prerequisites: Spike issues on bundle Rust API (rheo-l32) and cross-document labels (rheo-5tg) are now COMPLETE. Design can proceed immediately.

Goal: Produce a concrete architecture design for how rheo will use bundles.

== A. Terminology / config change ==
The 'copy' key is renamed to 'assets' everywhere in rheo.toml and in the Rust config types:
  - Global level:  assets = ["fonts/**", "images/**"]
  - Per-plugin:    [html]\n                 assets = ["style.css"]
  - Config structs: RheoConfig.copy -> RheoConfig.assets; PluginSection.copy -> PluginSection.assets; RheoConfigRaw.copy -> RheoConfigRaw.assets
  - The old 'copy' key should be rejected (or emit a deprecation warning) after rename.
  - This rename is independent and can be done as a separate task (tracked in NEW-A).

== B. TracedSpine design ==
Define a TracedSpine struct as the output of a pre-compilation tracing phase:

  TracedSpine {
    title: Option<String>,
    documents: Vec<SpineDocument>,  // ordered flat list
    assets: Vec<PathBuf>,           // all asset files (from toml + #asset() in sources)
    merge: bool,
  }

  SpineDocument {
    path: PathBuf,
    is_bundle_entry: bool,  // true if file contains #document() calls
  }

The tracer populates TracedSpine from two sources:
  1. rheo.toml spine vertebrae (glob patterns expanded to file list) and 'assets' globs
  2. Static parse of each vertebra .typ file for #document(path, ...) and #asset(...) calls
     using typst-syntax AST traversal (pre-compilation, no compilation needed)

== C. Ordering semantics ==
  - vertebrae order from rheo.toml takes precedence
  - within a glob pattern match: lexicographic by full file path
  - within a source file: top-to-bottom order of #document() declarations
  - files with no #document() calls are spine items themselves (no nesting)
  - if no vertebrae and no spine config: auto-discover all .typ files, sort lexicographically

== D. Hybrid user model ==
Two modes, both handled by the same tracer:

  rheo.toml-driven mode: User writes plain .typ files; rheo.toml lists vertebrae and assets.
    Tracer discovers files from rheo.toml, finds no #document() calls, treats each file as a
    direct document item (is_bundle_entry: false). Bundle entry generator wraps them in
    #document() calls.

  Source-driven mode: User's .typ file contains #document(...) calls.
    Tracer marks the file as a 'self-bundling entry' (is_bundle_entry: true). Bundle entry
    generator passes it through as-is — no wrapping applied. If a project mixes self-bundling
    and plain files, Rheo generates a combined bundle entry that passes through self-bundling
    files via #include and wraps plain files in #document() normally.

CONFIRMED DESIGN NOTE: If a .typ file has #document() calls, it is passed through as-is.
TracedSpine must track is_bundle_entry: bool per document so the generator knows not to wrap it.

== E. Assets merging ==
Final asset list = union of:
  - 'assets' glob patterns in rheo.toml (global and per-plugin)
  - #asset(name, ...) calls found by static analysis of vertebra files
Deduplication by resolved path. Order: rheo.toml assets first, then per-file declaration order.

== F. Merge semantics ==
  - merge=true (PDF): Generate a single #document() wrapping all vertebrae content
  - merge=false: Generate one #document() per vertebra

== G. EPUB scope — ANSWERED ==
EPUB is confirmed OUT OF SCOPE for bundle migration. The typst-bundle crate's DocumentFormat
enum has only two variants: Paged(PagedFormat) and Html. There is no EPUB variant.

Design decision: EPUB plugin stays on its current manual XHTML/zip path. However, if
BuiltSpine is removed as part of this refactor, the EPUB plugin must be adapted to not
depend on it. The EPUB plugin will need to call spine discovery (TracedSpine::trace)
directly and build its own HTML compile loop, rather than going through BuiltSpine.
Capture this as an explicit design decision: EPUB becomes an independent path.

== H. Single-file projects ==
A project with one .typ file should still use the bundle path (any source file in a rheo
project is 'bundled' format, as confirmed by user).

== I. Cargo.toml change required ==
The design must specify that typst-bundle needs to be added to both:
  - [workspace.dependencies] in the root Cargo.toml: typst-bundle = "0.14.2" (or current version)
  - [patch.crates-io] in root Cargo.toml: typst-bundle = { git = "https://github.com/typst/typst", branch = "main" }

Note: typst-bundle is a SEPARATE crate from typst — it is NOT included transitively through
the typst dependency. It must be explicitly added as a workspace dependency.

Document decisions in this issue's notes. The outcome feeds into rheo-3wr (TracedSpine impl),
rheo-18j (bundle entry generator), and indirectly all downstream implementation issues.
notes:
== J. Virtual file injection mechanism ==
Pre-populate world.slots before calling typst::compile::<Bundle>(). The slots field is
a Mutex<HashMap<FileId, Source>> (world.rs). Insert a Source built from the generated
bundle entry string keyed to a virtual FileId (e.g. VirtualPath::new("__rheo_bundle_entry__.typ")).
Because source() checks the cache first and returns on hit, this pre-populated entry is
returned as-is on first access, bypassing all disk reads and transformations.

== K. rheo_template injection for bundle entry ==
The world.rs source() method injects rheo.typ only for id == self.main. If the bundle
entry is pre-populated in slots, it bypasses source() entirely — so the injection path
never fires. Resolution: generate_bundle_entry() must bake the template preamble
directly into the generated string itself. The generated bundle entry must begin with:
  include_str!("typ/rheo.typ") + plugin_library_string + "#show: rheo_template\n\n"
followed by the #document() / #include calls. No runtime injection via world.rs needed.

== L. EPUB link transformer scope post-rheo-83v ==
rheo-83v removes the link transformer from the world.rs/compile.rs code paths. Scope
is limited to HTML and PDF bundle paths only. The EPUB plugin still needs .typ->/.xhtml
link rewriting and must call LinkTransformer directly within its own compile loop (not
via world.rs). rheo-83v must NOT delete transformer.rs until after EPUB is adapted.

== M. EPUB plugin adaptation gap ==
EPUB plugin (crates/epub/src/lib.rs) currently calls BuiltSpine::build() AND
generate_spine() separately. When BuiltSpine is removed (per Section G decision),
the EPUB plugin must be adapted to call TracedSpine::trace() for discovery and build
its own HTML compile loop. This is tracked as a separate feature issue blocked on rheo-3wr.
close_reason: Design complete: all 9 sections confirmed, 4 additional decisions documented in notes (J: virtual file injection, K: rheo_template baked into bundle entry, L: EPUB link transformer scope, M: EPUB adaptation gap). Downstream issues rheo-18j and rheo-3wr updated. New issue rheo-nci created for EPUB adaptation.

title: Refactor LinkTransformer to generic extension-based link replacement
description:
Remove hardcoded plugin name match arms from LinkTransformer and replace with a single generic extension-based rule.

Background: crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs lines 92-99 currently match on format names:
  ("html", _) => LinkTransform::ReplaceUrl { new_url: url.replace(TYP_EXT, HTML_EXT) },
  ("epub", _) => LinkTransform::ReplaceUrl { new_url: url.replace(TYP_EXT, XHTML_EXT) },
  _ => LinkTransform::KeepOriginal,

This couples the core transformer to specific plugin names. After the previous issues are complete, the EPUB plugin passes "xhtml" (not "epub") as the format name, and HTML passes "html". The pattern is simply: replace .typ with .{extension}.

Steps:

title: FormatPlugin trait lacks authoring contract documentation
description:
The `FormatPlugin` trait in `core/src/plugins.rs` has minimal doc comments. A plugin author cannot understand the full contract from the trait alone. Missing documentation:

**`name()`**: The return value serves triple duty — (1) the `--<name>` CLI flag, (2) the output subdirectory under `build/`, (3) the `format_name` passed to `RheoWorld` for link transformation and polyfill injection. Must be stable, lowercase, alphanumeric.

**`compile()`**: The critical `merge` ↔ `world` contract is documented only in `RheoCompileOptions`, not on the method itself:
- `ctx.spine.merge == true` → `ctx.options.input` and `ctx.options.world` are both `None`; the plugin builds its own worlds using `ctx.options.root` as the content root
- `ctx.spine.merge == false` → `ctx.options.input` is `Some(path)` and `ctx.options.world` is `Some(world)`, pre-initialised for that file
- Errors should be returned as `Err`, not swallowed; the CLI records failures and continues other files

**`inputs()`**: paths are relative to `ProjectConfig::root`; the CLI copies each resolved file to `plugin_output_dir` before calling `compile()`; `ctx.inputs` maps key names to source paths (not destination paths — see separate bug); missing optional inputs are absent from `ctx.inputs`; missing required inputs abort before `compile()` is called.

**`apply_defaults()`**: called when no `[plugin_name]` section exists in rheo.toml (currently — see related bug); `section` is a fresh default `PluginSection`; use to infer titles, set spine defaults, etc.

**`open()`**: called only when `--open` is passed; `OpenHandle::Server(h)` — caller calls `h.reload()` after each successful recompile in watch mode; `OpenHandle::Direct` — CLI opens files with system handler; `OpenHandle::None` — no action.

**`PluginSection::extra`**: explain the pattern for reading format-specific config with an example showing `section.extra.get("key").and_then(|v| v.as_str())`.

Fix: Expand doc comments on each method with the contract above. Also add a module-level doc comment in `plugins.rs` giving a "implementing a new plugin" walkthrough covering: implement the trait, add to `all_plugins()` in cli, add `[plugin_name]` section to rheo.toml reference.

title: Fix PDF merged compilation to handle per-document bibliographies
description:
## Background

`compile_pdf_merged_bundle()` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:46`) intentionally wraps all spine files in a single `#document("title.pdf")[#include "a.typ" #include "b.typ" ...]` bundle entry to produce one combined PDF. This fails with "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported" when multiple spine files each declare their own `#bibliography()`.

Unlike the per-file cases (rheo-o6h, rheo-j6j), merged mode cannot be fixed by simply compiling each file independently — the output must be a single combined PDF document.

## Options to evaluate

### Option A: Compile each vertebra independently then concatenate PDFs

Compile each spine file to a `PagedDocument` using `world.compile_pdf()` (available on `RheoWorld` at `crates/core/src/world.rs:269`). Concatenate the resulting documents into a single PDF.

Check whether `typst-pdf` provides a multi-document merge/concatenate API:
- Inspect the `typst-pdf` crate's public API for any concat/merge function.
- If it exists, use it to produce the merged PDF from individually compiled `PagedDocument`s.

### Option B: Require a single bundle-entry file for merged mode

If PDF concatenation is not available from `typst-pdf`, document the limitation and return a clear user-facing error when `merge=true` and the spine contains more than one non-bundle-entry document with a bibliography. The message should explain the workaround: create a single bundle-entry `.typ` that `#include`s all files and declares one shared `#bibliography()`.

## Implementation

1. Check the `typst-pdf` crate API. Look for any function that takes multiple `PagedDocument` values or accepts a list of pages from multiple sources.
2. If Option A is viable:
   - For each `doc` in `spine.documents`, create a `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`, inject a per-file bundle entry (single-document TracedSpine), call `world.compile_pdf()` to get a `PagedDocument`.
   - Use the concatenation API to merge all `PagedDocument`s.
   - Serialise to bytes with `document_to_pdf_bytes()` (check `crates/core/src/compile.rs` for existing helpers) and write to `output_path`.
3. If Option B:
   - Before calling `export_bundle()`, inspect whether any spine document declares a bibliography (this may require scanning source text or simply catching the Typst error and re-surfacing a better message).
   - Or: replace the current opaque "bundle compilation had errors: multiple bibliographies..." error with an explicit check and a message like: "Merged PDF does not support multiple bibliographies. Create a single entry file that #includes all chapters and declares one shared #bibliography()."

## Acceptance criteria

Option A: `cargo run -- compile examples/blog_site --pdf` with `merge = true` in rheo.toml produces one combined PDF with all bibliographies rendered.

Option B: The same command fails with a clear, actionable error message explaining the limitation and how to resolve it (not the raw Typst error).

Either way: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` pass.
close_reason: Done -- Merged PDF mode now works with context-wrapped bibliographies. Removed obsolete test_pdf_merge_duplicate_filenames test.

title: Simplify `PluginContext` by removing the `PluginConfig` wrapper and renaming fields
description:
## Problem
`PluginContext` in `crates/core/src/plugins.rs:48-58` passes the spine configuration twice:
- `plugin_config: PluginConfig { spine: SpineOptions { title, vertebrae, merge: bool } }` — resolved
- `plugin_section: PluginSection { spine: Option<UniversalSpine> }` — raw

`PluginConfig` is a single-field wrapper over `SpineOptions` that adds no value. The PDF plugin reads both `ctx.plugin_config.spine.merge` to branch, then `ctx.plugin_section.spine.as_ref()` for the actual config — duplicate data, inconsistent access.

## Fix
Remove `PluginConfig` entirely. Flatten `PluginContext`:

```rust
pub struct PluginContext<'a> {
    pub project: &'a ProjectConfig,
    pub output_config: &'a OutputConfig,
    pub options: RheoCompileOptions<'a>,
    pub spine: SpineOptions,       // was: plugin_config.spine
    pub config: PluginSection,     // was: plugin_section
    pub inputs: HashMap<&'static str, PathBuf>,
}
```

Update all call sites:
- `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`: construct `PluginContext` with `spine:` and `config:`; remove `PluginConfig` construction; remove `PluginConfig` from re-exports in `lib.rs`
- `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`: `ctx.plugin_config.spine.merge` → `ctx.spine.merge`; `ctx.plugin_section.spine` → `ctx.config.spine`
- `crates/html/src/lib.rs`: `ctx.plugin_config.spine.merge` → `ctx.spine.merge`; `ctx.plugin_section` → `ctx.config`
- `crates/epub/src/lib.rs`: `ctx.plugin_section` → `ctx.config`

## Key files
- `crates/core/src/plugins.rs`
- `crates/core/src/lib.rs` (remove PluginConfig from re-exports)
- `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`

- `crates/epub/src/lib.rs`

title: Unify package resolution: support all Typst namespaces in [plugin].packages
description:
## Background

rheo currently hard-codes `@preview` as the only resolvable namespace in `[plugin].packages`. `resolve_packages` (`crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:278-337`) rejects any `@<ns>/<name>:<ver>` spec where `<ns> != "preview"` (see line 309-313). This is asymmetric with the auto-detect path introduced by the manifest-packages feature (rheo-6j3, rheo-9dl, rheo-1hf, rheo-fal) and, more importantly, narrower than Typst itself: Typst resolves any namespace it can find under its package directories (`~/.local/share/typst/packages/<ns>/<name>/<ver>/` and `~/.cache/typst/packages/<ns>/<name>/<ver>/`).

After this issue, any namespace Typst itself can resolve from those directories must be valid in `[plugin].packages` — `@preview`, `@rheo`, `@local`, arbitrary user-defined namespaces. The explicit-declaration path should be gated only on whether the package is present locally, not on its namespace.

## Steps

1. Replace the inline `@preview/<name>:<version>` parsing in `resolve_packages` (`crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:285-313`) with a call to `find_local_package_dir` (introduced by rheo-9dl). Drop the namespace == "preview" check entirely. Any spec that `find_local_package_dir` resolves is valid; specs that don't resolve return `Err(RheoError::project_config(...))` with a message naming the spec and the directories searched, so users can debug cache state.

2. Preserve the strict error behaviour of `resolve_packages`: malformed specs (no `@`, no `/`, no `:`, empty parts) and missing packages still return `Err`. Only the auto-detect entry point (`find_package_in_dirs` consumers) silently skips unresolved specs.

3. Update CLAUDE.md's `rheo.toml` reference: drop any wording that implies `@preview` is special. The `packages` field now accepts any `@<ns>/<name>:<ver>` Typst itself can resolve from its package directories, plus relative paths.

4. Update tests to cover non-preview namespace resolution via the explicit path (e.g. `@rheo/...`, `@local/...`, arbitrary).

## Acceptance criteria

- `[html] packages = ["@rheo/slides:0.1.0"]` resolves the same package as `#import "@rheo/slides:0.1.0"`.
- `[html] packages = ["@local/foo:1.0.0"]` resolves correctly if `~/.local/share/typst/packages/local/foo/1.0.0/` exists.
- `[html] packages = ["@<arbitrary>/<name>:<ver>"]` works for any namespace, gated only on whether the package is present in the Typst package directories.
- Malformed or missing packages from `[plugin].packages` still produce a clear `RheoError` that names the spec and the searched directories.
- `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Fix PDF per-file plugin to compile each spine vertebra as a standalone document
description:
## Background

Same root cause as rheo-o6h (HTML plugin fix). The PDF per-file plugin (`compile_pdf_per_file_bundle()` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:72`) calls `world.export_bundle()` on the same combined world that wraps all spine documents in one `typst::compile::<Bundle>()` pass. When multiple spine files each declare `#bibliography()`, Typst raises "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported" and compilation fails.

The fix is the same pattern as for HTML: iterate over `spine.documents` and compile each file with its own `RheoWorld`, rather than using the pre-built combined world.

## Implementation

1. **Pass the full context into `compile_pdf_bundle_impl()`.** Currently `PdfPlugin::compile()` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:25`) passes only `ctx.options.world`, `ctx.options.output`, and `ctx.spine.merge` to `compile_pdf_bundle_impl()`. Extend the signature to also pass `ctx.spine` (a `&TracedSpine`) and `ctx.options.root` (the compilation root `&Path`).

2. **Refactor `compile_pdf_per_file_bundle()` to iterate per document** instead of calling `world.export_bundle()` once. For each `doc` in `spine.documents`:
   a. Create a fresh `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`. The `PdfPlugin.typst_library()` returns a small lemma helper — retrieve it via `PdfPlugin.typst_library()` and pass it through.
   b. Generate a per-file bundle entry via `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) for just this single document (single-document `TracedSpine`, `merge=false`). Inject it with `world.inject_bundle_entry()`.

title: Fix RheoConfig::has_format allocating a String for a contains check
description:
## Background

`crates/core/src/config.rs:190` has a needless heap allocation:


## Expected outcome
No heap allocation when checking if a format is configured. The fix is idiomatic Rust and avoids unnecessary `to_string()` calls in hot paths like plugin filtering.

title: Design: EPUB per-file target() polyfill after format_name removal
description:
Background: rheo-6wb removes format_name from RheoWorld. The target() polyfill currently lives in world.rs source() (lines ~251-256) and injects '#let target() = if ...' into every compiled file. rheo-t0f moves this polyfill into the bundle entry generator — correct for HTML and PDF. However, EPUB is explicitly out of scope for bundle compilation: it compiles each .typ file individually with its own RheoWorld instance (in EpubItem::create_from_source()). After format_name removal, EPUB per-file worlds will have no target() injected — user .typ files using '#if target() == "epub"' will break silently.

No existing issue addresses this gap.

Relevant files:
  crates/core/src/world.rs — current target() injection via format_name (lines ~251-256)
  crates/epub/src/lib.rs — EpubItem::create_from_source() where per-file worlds are created
  crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs — generate_bundle_entry() (rheo-18j)

== Decision Required ==

Who is responsible for injecting '#let target() = "epub"' into EPUB per-file compilations?

Option A (RECOMMENDED): EpubItem::create_from_source() prepends the polyfill to the source
string before passing it to compile_html_to_document(). This is self-contained in the EPUB
plugin and does not require world.rs changes.

  Concrete implementation:
    let polyfill = "#let target() = \"epub\"\n\n";
    let source_with_polyfill = format!("{}{}", polyfill, original_source);
    // pass source_with_polyfill to compile_html_to_document()

Option B: Keep a lightweight per-file polyfill injection in world.rs for non-bundle paths.
This contradicts the goal of removing format_name from world.rs and is NOT preferred.

== Accepted Resolution ==

Use Option A. EpubItem::create_from_source() prepends '#let target() = "epub"\n\n' to
each source string. This is the minimal change, keeps the EPUB plugin self-contained, and
requires no world.rs involvement.

Implementation steps:
1. In crates/epub/src/lib.rs, locate EpubItem::create_from_source() (or equivalent).
2. Before passing source to compile_html_to_document(), prepend:
     let source = format!("#let target() = \"epub\"\n\n{}", source);
3. Confirm that world.rs no longer needs to inject the polyfill for EPUB paths.
4. Run RUN_EPUB_TESTS=1 cargo test --test harness — EPUB tests must pass.
5. Verify that '#if target() == "epub" [...]' works correctly in a test .typ file.

Acceptance criteria:
- EPUB .typ files can call target() and get the string 'epub'
- world.rs does not inject any per-format polyfill on the EPUB path
- All EPUB tests pass
close_reason: Fixed EPUB target() polyfill injection for module files. Changed condition from checking self.main in slots to checking if main file is NOT a .typ file (EPUB uses temp files). All 38 EPUB tests pass.

title: Isolate test_html_css_link_injection to avoid mutating shared examples directory
description:
## Background

The test `test_html_css_link_injection` (harness.rs:453-558) compiles the shared `../../examples/blog_site` project **in place**, writing to its `build/` directory, then calls `rheo clean` to clean up. This is not isolated: if the test fails before the cleanup `rheo clean`, the shared example is left in a compiled state.

More importantly, this test compiles directly into the examples directory rather than into a test store, which means:
- If tests run in parallel, another test that also uses `examples/blog_site` (e.g. the parametrised `run_test_case` for `../../examples/blog_site`) can race with this test.
- The explicit `rheo clean` before compile (lines 458-475) also cleans any existing build artifacts from the parametrised test run, breaking its isolation too.

## Correct Pattern

Other tests in the same file that need a project with specific properties use `tempfile::tempdir()` (e.g. `test_html_custom_stylesheet_inlined` at line 562). For tests that need an existing project, the parametrised test harness uses `copy_project_to_test_store()`.

   ```rust
   let test_dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("Failed to create temp dir");
   copy_project_to_test_store(\u0026test_case.project_path(), test_dir.path())
       .expect("Failed to copy project");
   let project_path = test_dir.path();
   ```

2. Remove the initial `rheo clean` call (lines 458-475) — the temp copy starts clean.

3. Update the compile command to use the temp path instead of the original examples path.

4. Update the HTML file path assertions to read from `test_dir.path().join("build/html/index.html")` (or use `--build-dir` flag pointing inside the temp dir).

5. Remove the final `rheo clean` call — cleanup is automatic via `tempdir` drop.

## Expected Outcome

`test_html_css_link_injection` no longer touches `examples/blog_site/build/`. The test is fully isolated and can run concurrently with the parametrised blog_site test case.

title: Replace ad-hoc directory creation in procedural tests with tempfile
description:
## Background

Two integration tests in `crates/tests/tests/harness.rs` create their test fixture directories using hardcoded relative paths instead of `tempfile::tempdir()`. This creates several problems: the paths may land in unintended locations relative to the test binary's CWD, directories can survive if a test panics before cleanup, and parallel test runs can conflict.

## Affected Tests

**`test_pdf_merge_link_not_in_spine`** — `harness.rs:328-384`
```rust
let test_dir = PathBuf::from("tests/cases/pdf_merge_error_nonspine");
std::fs::create_dir_all(\u0026test_dir)...
```

**`test_pdf_merge_duplicate_filenames`** — `harness.rs:388-449`
```rust
let test_dir = PathBuf::from("tests/cases/pdf_merge_error_duplicate");
```

These relative paths resolve to `{cwd}/tests/cases/...`, which from `crates/tests/` package root would be inside the `tests/` subdirectory — an odd location next to `tests/harness.rs` itself. The cleanup is `std::fs::remove_dir_all(\u0026test_dir).ok()` called *after* the assertion that might panic, leaving the directory behind on test failure.

## Comparison with Good Tests

The test `test_html_custom_stylesheet_inlined` (harness.rs:562) uses `tempfile::tempdir()` correctly — the directory is automatically cleaned up even on panic.

## Implementation Steps

1. In `test_pdf_merge_link_not_in_spine`, replace:
   ```rust
   let test_dir = PathBuf::from("tests/cases/pdf_merge_error_nonspine");
   std::fs::create_dir_all(\u0026test_dir)...
   // ... cleanup at end ...
   std::fs::remove_dir_all(\u0026test_dir).ok();
   ```
   with:
   ```rust
   let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("Failed to create temp dir");
   let test_dir = dir.path();
   // ... (no explicit cleanup needed, tempdir drops on scope exit)
   ```
   Also update `test_dir.join("rheo.toml")`, `test_dir.join("intro.typ")`, etc. to use `test_dir.to_str().unwrap()` where needed.

2. Apply the same transformation to `test_pdf_merge_duplicate_filenames`. The subdirectory creation (`let dir1 = test_dir.join("dir1")`) still works when `test_dir` is a temp path.

3. Update the cargo compile commands in both tests: currently they use `cargo run -- compile ...` without the `-p rheo-cli` flag (compare with other tests that use `cargo run -p rheo-cli -- compile ...`). Standardise to use `-p rheo-cli`.

## Expected Outcome

Both tests are self-contained, use temporary directories, and leave no filesystem artifacts after success or failure.
close_reason: Replaced ad-hoc directory creation with tempfile in test_pdf_merge_link_not_in_spine and test_pdf_merge_duplicate_filenames

title: Fix HTML plugin to compile each spine vertebra as a standalone document
description:
## Background

When compiling a project where multiple spine vertebrae each declare `#bibliography()`, the HTML plugin fails with Typst's error: "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported". This is a regression caused by how the HTML plugin uses the bundle API.

The HTML plugin's `compile_html_bundle()` (`crates/html/src/lib.rs:117`) calls `options.world.export_bundle()`. That world was assembled by `compile_with_bundle()` in `crates/cli/src/orchestrate.rs:52-103`. It injects a synthetic bundle entry generated by `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) that wraps every spine document in the project in a single `typst::compile::<Bundle>()` call:

```
#document("severance-ep-1.html")[#include "severance-ep-1.typ"]
#document("severance-ep-2.html")[#include "severance-ep-2.typ"]
...
```

Because all files are pulled into one compilation pass, Typst sees multiple `#bibliography()` declarations and errors. The correct behaviour is that each spine vertebra is an independent entrypoint compiled with its own `RheoWorld` — exactly as the EPUB plugin already does in `compile_epub_impl()` (`crates/epub/src/lib.rs:322-356`), where it iterates `spine.documents` and compiles each file independently.

## Implementation

1. **Pass spine info into the compile function.** Modify `HtmlPlugin::compile()` (`crates/html/src/lib.rs:102`) to pass `ctx.spine` and `ctx.options.root` (compilation root) into `compile_html_bundle()`. Currently only `ctx.options` and `ctx.config` are passed; the spine is needed to iterate documents.

2. **Refactor `compile_html_bundle()` to iterate per document** instead of calling `options.world.export_bundle()` once for everything. The new loop body for each `doc` in `spine.documents`:
   a. Build a single-document `TracedSpine` (`merge=false`, single entry with `doc`) — or just pass the document path directly.
   b. Create a fresh `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`. The `plugin_library` is `HtmlPlugin.typst_library()` (which returns `None` for HTML — check `crates/html/src/lib.rs`).
   c. Generate a per-file bundle entry via `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) for just this one document, then inject it with `world.inject_bundle_entry()`.
   d. Call `world.export_bundle()` to produce HTML output for this one file.
   e. Apply the existing CSS/font injection logic to each `.html` file in the output (code currently at `crates/html/src/lib.rs:141-171` — reuse it unchanged).
   f. Write output files to `options.output` directory (unchanged).

3. **Handle `is_bundle_entry=true` documents** (the `SpineDocument.is_bundle_entry` flag). For these, create a `RheoWorld` pointing directly to the file without adding a `#document()` wrapper — the file controls its own bundle structure. Generate the bundle entry with a `TracedSpine` that includes only this one `is_bundle_entry=true` document (spine.rs already handles this case by emitting a bare `#include`).

4. The combined `options.world` (the old all-files world created by `compile_with_bundle()` in orchestrate.rs) is **not used** in the refactored path. Ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo run -- compile examples/blog_site --html` succeeds with no errors.
- One `.html` file is produced in the output directory per spine vertebra.
- Each file's bibliography renders correctly (citations resolve within the individual document).
- `cargo test` passes.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.
close_reason: Fixed HTML plugin to compile each spine vertebra independently with its own RheoWorld, resolving multiple bibliographies issue.

title: Add bundle field to PluginSection in core config
description:
## Background

The HTML plugin uses Typst's bundle API (compiling all spine files in a single Typst session via typst::compile::<Bundle>). This causes 'multiple bibliographies are not yet supported' errors when multiple .typ files each have their own #bibliography() call, because Typst sees all bibliography calls in the same compilation — even across separate #document() scopes.

The fix is to add a bundle: Option<bool> field to PluginSection in crates/core/src/config.rs. This allows users to opt out of bundle compilation per-plugin in rheo.toml. When bundle = false, the CLI routes to per-file compilation where each .typ file is compiled independently with its own RheoWorld.

## File to edit

crates/core/src/config.rs

## Task

Add bundle: Option<bool> to the PluginSection struct (around line 36):

```rust
pub struct PluginSection {
    pub spine: Option<Spine>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "copy")]
    pub assets: Vec<String>,
    /// Override bundle API usage for this plugin.
    /// None = use plugin's built-in default (uses_bundle_api()).
    /// false = per-file compilation (each .typ file compiled independently).
    /// true = Typst bundle API (all files in one compilation session).
    pub bundle: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(flatten, default)]
    pub extra: toml::Table,
}
```

This field uses serde's named field priority over flatten — the same pattern as spine and assets. When bundle = false is set in rheo.toml under [html], it will be parsed into PluginSection.bundle = Some(false) and will NOT appear in extra.

## Expected outcome

- cargo test passes (existing tests unaffected; no tests assert on PluginSection layout)
- cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes
- [html]\nbundle = false in rheo.toml is parsed correctly
- Default behaviour (bundle absent or bundle = true) is unchanged

title: PluginContext should borrow spine/config/assets instead of cloning them per file
description:
## Background

`PluginContext` (defined in `crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:61–92`) takes three fields by owned value:

```rust
pub struct PluginContext<'a> {
    pub spine: SpineOptions,
    pub config: PluginSection,
    pub assets: HashMap<&'static str, Asset>,
    // ... other fields are already references
}
```

In per-file compilation mode (`crates/cli/src/lib.rs:472–503`), `compile_one_file` is called once per .typ file per plugin. Each call constructs a new `PluginContext`, which requires cloning `spine`, `config`, and `assets` — data that is identical across all files in the same plugin batch. For a project with 10 files and 3 plugins that is 30 unnecessary clones.

The struct already has a lifetime `'a` (used for `options`, `project`, and `output_config`), so adding borrow fields is natural.

The root cause is in `compile_one_file` at `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:317–319`:
```rust
let ctx = PluginContext {
    project: pfc.project,
    output_config: pfc.output_config,
    options,
    spine: pfc.spine.clone(),            // line 317
    config: pfc.plugin_section.clone(),   // line 318
    assets: pfc.resolved_assets.clone(),  // line 319
};
```

`pfc` (`PerFileCtx`) already holds these as references (`&'a SpineOptions` etc). The clone exists only to satisfy `PluginContext`'s ownership requirement.

## Relevant files
- `crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs` — `PluginContext` struct definition (lines 61–92)
- `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` — `compile_one_file` (lines 300–329), `PerFileCtx` (lines 286–294)
- `crates/rheo-html/src/lib.rs` — constructs and reads `PluginContext`
- `crates/rheo-pdf/src/lib.rs` — constructs and reads `PluginContext`
- `crates/rheo-epub/src/lib.rs` — constructs and reads `PluginContext`

## Implementation steps

1. In `crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs`, change `PluginContext<'a>` fields:
   ```rust
   pub spine: &'a SpineOptions,
   pub config: &'a PluginSection,
   pub assets: &'a HashMap<&'static str, Asset>,
   ```

2. In `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` in `compile_one_file`, remove the three `.clone()` calls:
   ```rust
   let ctx = PluginContext {
       project: pfc.project,
       output_config: pfc.output_config,
       options,
       spine: pfc.spine,            // was: pfc.spine.clone()
       config: pfc.plugin_section,  // was: pfc.plugin_section.clone()
       assets: pfc.resolved_assets, // was: pfc.resolved_assets.clone()
   };
   ```

3. In the merged-mode `PluginContext` construction (around `lib.rs:454–461`), `spine` and `resolved_assets` are created locally and moved in. These moves are still valid — no change needed there.

4. Fix any compile errors in plugin crates that read these fields. The fields change from owned to borrowed, so any code that tries to move out of them (e.g., `ctx.spine.title`) will need to clone or borrow (`ctx.spine.title.clone()` or `ctx.spine.title.as_deref()`).

5. Run `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` to confirm.

## Expected outcome
No per-file cloning of spine/config/assets in per-file compilation mode. The owned-value form is only used in the merged-mode path where the values are local anyway.
close_reason: Changed PluginContext fields spine/config/assets from owned to borrowed (&'a). Removed per-file clones in per-file mode.

Update and add integration tests to verify the deferred auto-detection flow works correctly, including a genuine first-compile scenario.

## Background
The existing e2e test `e2e_auto_detected_manifest_package_assets` in `crates/tests/tests/manifest_packages.rs:79` pre-populates `XDG_CACHE_HOME` with the package before running compile. It should still pass after the refactoring (same flow, deferred execution).

We also need:
- a test for explicit packages,
- a test for `auto_detect_packages = false`,
- a test that genuinely exercises the first-compile-after-download path (the core bug the refactor fixes).

## Steps

1. Open `crates/tests/tests/manifest_packages.rs`. Verify the existing e2e test still passes.

2. Add `explicit_packages_in_rheo_toml_still_resolved`:
   - Set up a project with explicit `[html] packages = ["@testns/testpkg:0.1.0"]` in rheo.toml.
   - Pre-cache the package (with a `[tool.rheo.html]` section in its typst.toml).
   - Compile and assert the CSS/JS appear in the output directory and are referenced in the HTML.

3. Add `auto_detect_packages_false_skips_detection`:
   - Set up a project with `auto_detect_packages = false` under `[html]` in rheo.toml.
   - Include a `@preview/...` import in a .typ file with package having `[tool.rheo.html]` assets.
   - Pre-cache the package.
   - Compile and assert the package assets do NOT appear in the output directory and are NOT referenced in the HTML.

4. Add `auto_detect_finds_package_after_first_compile_downloads_it` — the test that actually exercises the new code path:

```text
Strategy (no mock registry required):
- Tempdir A is XDG_CACHE_HOME. Initially empty (no packages cached).
- Tempdir B is the project directory with rheo.toml + a .typ file
  importing @testns/testpkg:0.1.0.
- Pre-stage the package files in a SEPARATE tempdir that Typst can
  treat as a local package directory by putting it under
  XDG_DATA_HOME instead of XDG_CACHE_HOME. (Typst searches data_dir
  before cache_dir per crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:301-374.)
  This simulates "Typst sees the package" without simulating a
  network download.
- BEFORE the first compile: assert that
  build_auto_detected_package_blocks(...) (or, equivalently, calling
  detect_manifest_package_assets directly with no manifest scan)
  WOULD find the package — we need to set up a state where the
  pre-compile scan does not have visibility, then post-compile does.

Simpler equivalent: invoke the rheo CLI twice — first compile
populates an XDG cache, then delete the build/ output (NOT the
cache), and run compile again. The second run is a "compile against
populated cache" which is what the existing test does. But by running
the FIRST compile against an empty cache and asserting it ALSO
succeeds (assets appear in output), we exercise the deferred flow.
```

Concretely:
- Use `XDG_DATA_HOME=<tempdir>` pre-populated with `typst/packages/testns/testpkg/0.1.0/...` so Typst finds the package without a network call, but **`XDG_CACHE_HOME=<empty tempdir>`** so the project's first-compile cache is empty.
- Run `rheo compile` once.
- Assert: build/html/testns/testpkg/index.css exists AND build/html/<name>.html contains `<link ... href="testns/testpkg/index.css">`.
- This proves that the deferred resolve+inject flow works end-to-end without relying on rheo's old "resolve before compile" path: the first invocation of resolve_assets sees no auto-detected packages until the post-compile phase.

Add a comment at the top of the test explaining the strategy.

## Anti-pattern (do NOT do this)
The original phrasing of this issue proposed a "pre-populate the cache dir but verify the deferred flow works" test. That's tautological — it doesn't exercise the bug. Use the data_dir-vs-cache_dir split above, or run two consecutive compiles, to make the test meaningful.

## References
- Existing e2e test: `crates/tests/tests/manifest_packages.rs:79`
- Typst package search order (data_dir, then cache_dir, then explicit dir): `crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:301-374`
- `detect_manifest_package_assets_in_dirs`: `crates/core/src/plugins/typst_manifest.rs:112-122`
- Test harness patterns: other files in `crates/tests/tests/`

## Expected outcome
Four tests pass: existing e2e, explicit-packages, auto_detect_packages=false, and the genuine first-compile test. `cargo test --test manifest_packages` succeeds.
close_reason: Superseded by rheo-0d3p, which scopes the test suite to the pre-warm flow. The new test issue keeps the explicit-packages and auto_detect=false cases, drops the unsound 'first-compile' test, and adds a real first-compile test via XDG_DATA_HOME staging with an empty XDG_CACHE_HOME.

title: Extract `compile_one_file()` helper to eliminate duplication in `perform_compilation()`
description:
## Problem
`perform_compilation()` in `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:341-454` has three nearly-identical blocks that all create a `PluginContext` and call `plugin.compile()`:
1. Merge mode: creates temp world, calls compile once (~40 lines)

3. Per-file, fresh world: loops, creates fresh world, creates ctx (~32 lines)

Extract a private helper that takes a `&mut RheoWorld`, builds `RheoCompileOptions` and `PluginContext`, calls `plugin.compile()`, and returns `Result<()>`:

```rust
fn compile_one_file<'a>(
    plugin: &dyn FormatPlugin,
    typ_file: &Path,
    output_path: &Path,
    project: &'a ProjectConfig,
    output_config: &'a OutputConfig,
    world: &'a mut RheoWorld,
    spine: SpineOptions,
    config: PluginSection,
    inputs: HashMap<&'static str, PathBuf>,
) -> Result<()>
```

The two per-file loops then both call this helper, differing only in how they obtain `&mut world`.

title: [core] Replace lazy_static! with std::sync::LazyLock in constants.rs
description:
crates/core/src/constants.rs uses the lazy_static external crate (line 2) for three regex statics. std::sync::LazyLock has been stable since Rust 1.80 (July 2024) and provides identical functionality without the external dependency.

Steps:
1. In crates/core/src/constants.rs, replace each:
   ```rust
   lazy_static! {
       pub static ref X: T = expr;
   }
   ```


2. Replace `use lazy_static::lazy_static;` with `use std::sync::LazyLock;`

title: ctx.inputs maps to source paths, not copied destination paths
description:
`cli/src/lib.rs:362` inserts the *source* path into `resolved_inputs` after copying the file to the output directory:

    std::fs::copy(&src, &dest).map_err(...)?;
    resolved_inputs.insert(input.name, src);  // src, not dest

A plugin receiving `ctx.inputs["stylesheet"]` gets the project-root path, not the path to the copy in the plugin's output directory. If a plugin then reads the file from `ctx.inputs`, it's reading from the project (which is fine for reading), but if it needs to reference the *output-side* path (e.g., to generate a relative link in the output file), it has the wrong path.

The HTML plugin doesn't use `ctx.inputs` at all (it reads stylesheets directly from `ctx.project.root` and the config), so this bug is currently latent. But the `inputs()` API is part of the `FormatPlugin` contract and will affect future plugins.

Fix: Insert the destination path:

    resolved_inputs.insert(input.name, dest);

Also update the `FormatPlugin::inputs()` documentation (see related issue) to clearly state that `ctx.inputs` values are paths in the plugin's output directory.
close_reason: Now inserts destination path into resolved_inputs instead of source path

title: Fix reference path resolution broken for 'cases/' integration tests
description:
## Background

The integration test harness recently adopted a 'test store' pattern where each test project is copied to a temporary `store/{name}/` directory before compilation. This introduced a regression: both the reference *verification* path and the reference *update/generation* path now resolve to the wrong location for tests under `crates/tests/cases/`.

## Root Cause

**File:** `crates/tests/src/helpers/comparison.rs:93-100`
**File:** `crates/tests/src/helpers/reference.rs:73-80`

Both `get_reference_dir` (used when verifying) and `get_project_ref_dir` (used when updating with UPDATE_REFERENCES=1) decide between `ref/cases/` and `ref/examples/` with:

```rust
if project_path.starts_with("tests/cases/") {
    PathBuf::from("ref/cases")
} else if project_path.starts_with("examples/") {
    PathBuf::from("ref/examples")
} else {
    PathBuf::from("ref/examples")  // fallback
}
```

Before the test-store refactor, `project_path` (or `actual_dir`) was the original case path such as `cases/bundle_cross_doc_labels`. Now it is `store/bundle_cross_doc_labels` (set at harness.rs:85: `project_path = test_store.clone()`).

Neither `"store/..."` variant matches `"tests/cases/"` or `"examples/"`, so both functions always fall through to `ref/examples/`. This means:
- Verification looks at `ref/examples/bundle_cross_doc_labels/html` (does not exist)
- `ensure_reference_exists` panics: `"HTML reference not found for bundle_cross_doc_labels. Run with UPDATE_REFERENCES=1 to generate."`

The existing references committed to the repo are at `ref/cases/bundle_cross_doc_labels/html/` and `ref/cases/bundle_document_entries/html/` — they are in the correct location but the code no longer finds them.

## Affected Tests

- `cases/bundle_cross_doc_labels` — HTML refs at `ref/cases/bundle_cross_doc_labels/html/`, would panic during verify
- `cases/bundle_document_entries` — HTML refs at `ref/cases/bundle_document_entries/html/`, would panic during verify
- Any future test added under `cases/` would be silently miscategorised

## Implementation Steps

1. **Identify the test origin from its name**, not the store path.

   In `harness.rs`, the test case is created with the original path (e.g. `"cases/bundle_cross_doc_labels"`). The `original_project_path` variable (line 49) still holds this before it is moved to the store.

2. **Pass `original_project_path` to the reference functions** instead of (or in addition to) the store path.

   In `harness.rs`, change `update_html_references(test_name, &html_output, &project_path)` to pass `&original_project_path` as the third argument. Do the same for `update_pdf_references` and `update_epub_references`.

3. **Fix `get_reference_dir` in comparison.rs** to also accept an optional original project path, OR change it to determine the ref type from `test_name` alone. The simplest fix: the test names under cases use a predictable prefix — e.g. rename the cases to carry their origin. Alternatively, derive ref base from the original path passed via `TestCase`.

   A clean approach: expose `original_project_path` in `TestCase`, thread it to verify functions, and update the `starts_with` checks to use it:
   - `original_project_path.starts_with("cases/")` → `ref/cases`
   - `original_project_path.starts_with("examples/")` or `original_project_path.starts_with("../../examples/")` → `ref/examples`

4. **Run `cargo test --test harness`** to confirm bundle tests now find their refs and pass.

## Expected Outcome

`cargo test --test harness` for `bundle_cross_doc_labels` and `bundle_document_entries` cases resolves refs from `ref/cases/` and passes without panic. Future tests under `cases/` also correctly use `ref/cases/`.
close_reason: Fixed reference path resolution to use original_project_path for determining ref/cases/ vs ref/examples/

title: Design: Move target() polyfill from world.rs into bundle entry generator
description:
Background: RheoWorld.format_name is removed in rheo-6wb. That field currently drives the target() polyfill injection in world.rs source() (lines 251-256 of crates/core/src/world.rs):

  let target_polyfill = if self.format_name.is_some() {
      '// Polyfill target() ...\n#let target() = if "rheo-target" in sys.inputs { sys.inputs.rheo-target } else { std.target() }\n\n'
  } else { '' };

When format_name is removed, this injection disappears. But user Typst files use target() to branch per-format (e.g., '#if target() == "html" [...]'). We must keep it working.

Relevant files:
  crates/core/src/world.rs — current target() injection (lines ~251-256)
  crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs — where generate_bundle_entry() will live (rheo-18j)

== Solution ==

generate_bundle_entry(traced: &TracedSpine, format: &str, plugin_library: &str) -> String
(from rheo-18j) must emit the target() polyfill at the very TOP of the generated bundle
entry .typ, as the FIRST line — before rheo.typ, before plugin_library, before #show.

  // Generated by rheo — do not edit
  #let target() = "html"  // or "pdf", "epub" — substituted from the format arg

NOTE: This is a static string substitution (not sys.inputs lookup) because the bundle entry
is generated per-format. The format is known at generation time, so we can emit it directly.
This is simpler and does not require sys.inputs to be configured.

The old sys.inputs approach (sys.inputs.rheo-target) can be removed from world.rs once this
is in place. The format arg passed to generate_bundle_entry() is the plugin's name() value
(e.g., 'html', 'pdf', 'epub').

== Required preamble ordering in generate_bundle_entry() ==

The bundle entry string MUST be assembled in this exact order:
  1. #let target() = "<format>"\n\n        ← FIRST — must be in scope for rheo.typ
  2. {rheo.typ content}\n\n                 ← second
  3. {plugin_library}\n\n                   ← third
  4. #show: rheo_template\n\n               ← fourth
  5. document content (#include statements)  ← last

The target() polyfill MUST precede rheo.typ so it is in scope within the template's own
code. Placing it after #show: rheo_template or after rheo.typ is incorrect.

Implementation steps:
1. In crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs, at the TOP of the generated bundle entry string,
   add this line first, before everything else:
     format!("#let target() = \"{}\"\n\n", format)
   Then append: rheo.typ content, plugin_library, #show: rheo_template, then the document content.
2. In crates/core/src/world.rs, after rheo-6wb removes format_name:
   - Remove the target_polyfill injection block (lines ~251-256)
   - Remove build_inputs(format_name) logic that sets 'rheo-target' in sys.inputs (lines ~22-28)
   - Remove the format_name field and its parameter from RheoWorld::new()
3. Run cargo build and confirm no compile errors.
4. Test that '#if target() == "html" [...]' works correctly in a test .typ file.
   The integration test 'bundle_cross_doc_labels' (rheo-cbw) will cover this.

Acceptance criteria:
- generate_bundle_entry() emits '#let target() = "<format>"' as the FIRST line of its output
- world.rs no longer injects target() polyfill or sets rheo-target in sys.inputs
- cargo build succeeds
- target() returns the correct format string in compiled output

title: EpubPlugin ignores pre-resolved ctx.spine, re-reads raw config
description:
`EpubPlugin::compile()` receives `ctx.spine: SpineOptions` — the already-resolved title, vertebrae, and merge flag — but discards it entirely:

    epub/src/lib.rs:60-62
    fn compile(&self, ctx: PluginContext<'_>) -> Result<()> {
        compile_epub_new(ctx.options, ctx.config)  // ctx.spine never read
    }

`compile_epub_impl` then re-reads `section.spine` from the raw `PluginSection`, bypassing all the resolution logic in `perform_compilation` (cli/src/lib.rs:411-419), including:
- The `plugin.default_merge()` fallback
- The `spine_cfg.and_then(|s| s.merge)` unwrap
- The already-resolved vertebrae list

This means EPUB is the only plugin that doesn't honour the `SpineOptions` contract.

Fix: Align EPUB with the PDF plugin's approach — read from `ctx.spine` directly:
- Use `ctx.spine.title` for the package title
- Use `ctx.spine.vertebrae` to drive file discovery (or fall back to `generate_spine` with no config when empty)
- Use `ctx.spine.merge` (always true for EPUB given `default_merge()`) to confirm mode
- Pass the resolved `ctx.spine` into `compile_epub_impl` instead of the raw section

Also consider whether `section.extra` (identifier, date) should still be read from the raw config — yes, since those fields have no place in the generic `SpineOptions`. Only the spine fields need to move to `ctx.spine`.
close_reason: Implemented: EpubPlugin now uses ctx.spine instead of re-reading raw config, aligning with PDF plugin approach

title: Address PR #122 review feedback (multi-block [[plugin.assets]])
description:
Code review of PR #122 (multi-block [[plugin.assets]] support, branch ahead of main by 9 commits) surfaced the following items. Address each in a single follow-up branch unless noted.

PR: https://github.com/freecomputinglab/rheo/pull/122

## 1. BLOCKER — Broken slides example
File: examples/slides_html_pdf/rheo-slides/src/lib.ts:6
The hunk adds `import myStyle from './style.css?raw';` but `style.css` does not exist in that directory (only `lib.ts` and `rheo-slides.typ`) and `myStyle` is never referenced. This breaks the slides bundle. Drop this hunk from the PR entirely.

## 2. Nit — Stale doc comment on resolve_assets
File: crates/cli/src/lib.rs:398-399
Current text:
    /// Resolve plugin assets, collecting overrides across all [[plugin.assets]] blocks
    /// and dispatching to the declared combine strategy.
The `AssetCombine` trait was removed in 8a749d1 but this comment still references "the declared combine strategy". Replace the second line with something like: "and copying each source verbatim into the plugin output dir."

## 3. Nit — Misleading test name
File: crates/tests/tests/harness.rs:1080
`test_asset_multiple_blocks_default_combiner` references the removed combiner concept. Rename to `test_asset_multiple_blocks_inject_all` (or similar). No behavioural change.

## 4. SHOULD-FIX — Silent destination-path collisions across blocks
File: crates/cli/src/lib.rs (resolve_assets / copy_each, ~lines 369-450)
If two [[html.assets]] blocks declare the same effective path (e.g. both set `css_stylesheet = "style.css"`, or two paths that strip to the same relative dest), `copy_each` writes to the same `dest`, the second `std::fs::copy` overwrites the first, and the returned Vec<Asset> contains duplicate `built_relative_path` entries. The HTML plugin then emits duplicate <link> tags pointing at the same file.

Preferred fix: detect the collision in resolve_assets and return RheoError::project_config with a clear message naming the colliding asset and the two source paths. (Alternative: silently dedupe by built_relative_path — rejected because it hides user mistakes.)

Add a unit test in crates/cli/src/lib.rs covering two blocks with identical `built_relative_path` -> Err(project_config).

## 5. SHOULD-FIX — Panic on absolute override paths
File: crates/cli/src/lib.rs:374 (inside copy_each)
    let rel = src
        .strip_prefix(project_root)
        .expect("source is always project_root-joined");
PathBuf::join returns the right-hand side unchanged when it's absolute. So a user override like `css_stylesheet = "/tmp/foo.css"` makes `strip_prefix(project_root)` return Err and the `.expect` panics.

Fix: replace the panic with a RheoError::project_config explaining that asset override paths must be relative to the project root, naming the offending path. (Alternatively, validate at config load time — but the in-resolver check is cheaper to add and covers all entry points.)

Add a regression test passing an absolute override and asserting Err(project_config).

## 6. Nit — Tighten unwrap_or(&abs) in built_relative_path derivation
File: crates/cli/src/lib.rs:~434
    let rel = abs.strip_prefix(plugin_output_dir).unwrap_or(&abs)
              .to_string_lossy()
              .into_owned();
copy_each always returns paths under plugin_output_dir, so the fallback is unreachable today. If a future refactor breaks the invariant, this would silently emit an absolute disk path as the asset's built_relative_path, which the HTML plugin would render as a broken <link href>. Replace with `.expect("copy_each output is always under plugin_output_dir")` to fail loudly.

## 7. Optional — Unreachable Default for AssetsField
File: crates/core/src/config.rs (AssetsField impl Default)
PluginSection.assets is Option<AssetsField>, defaults to None, and asset_blocks() already handles None. The Default impl appears unreachable in normal flow. Verify whether serde derive requires it; if not, remove it.

## 8. Out-of-scope / discuss — JS-only-when-CSS coupling (pre-existing)
File: crates/html/src/lib.rs (compile, ~line 101+)
The `if let Some(css_assets) = …` branch is the only place JS gets injected. A project that supplies js_scripts but no css_stylesheet will silently get the default inline CSS and no JS. Pre-existing behaviour, but worth either splitting CSS and JS injection into independent branches in this PR, or filing as a separate issue and noting in the PR description.

## Verification
- `cargo build && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test` (covers existing harness tests + new regression tests for items 4 and 5)
- Manually run `cargo run -- compile examples/slides_html_pdf` to confirm the slides example builds after fix 1.
close_reason: Done

## Background

This issue adds tests for two features:
1. Reserved keyword validation: `AssetConfig.name` values of `"spine"` or `"assets"` are rejected (rheo-9od)
2. Configurable asset paths: users can override `AssetConfig.default_path` via the asset's `name` key in rheo.toml (rheo-a9l)

Thanks to architectural improvements in those issues, the core logic is now on well-defined, testable types rather than inline in `perform_compilation()`.

## Unit Tests

### `AssetConfig::validate()` — in `crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs`

Add a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block (or extend existing one):

1. **Reserved name "spine" rejected**: `AssetConfig { name: "spine", default_path: "x.css", required: false }.validate("test_plugin")` returns Err containing "spine"
2. **Reserved name "assets" rejected**: same with `name: "assets"`, returns Err containing "assets"
3. **Valid name accepted**: `AssetConfig { name: "css_stylesheet", default_path: "style.css", required: false }.validate("test_plugin")` returns Ok
4. **Error uses MisconfiguredPlugin variant**: verify the error variant is `RheoError::MisconfiguredPlugin`

### `PluginSection::get_string()` — in `crates/core/src/config.rs`

Add to existing test module:

1. **String value returned**: `[html]\ncss_stylesheet = "custom.css"` → `section.get_string("css_stylesheet") == Some("custom.css")`

### `resolve_assets()` — in `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`

1. **Default path used when no override**: plugin declares asset with `default_path: "style.css"`, create file at `project_root/style.css`, no config override → asset resolved with `built_relative_path == "style.css"`

title: Resolve asset overrides relative to package source_root
description:
Background: resolve_assets in crates/cli/src/lib.rs:416-526 resolves asset override paths (css_stylesheet, js_scripts, etc.) relative to project_root. Once packages can carry their own asset overrides (rh-C makes the HTML plugin able to set css_stylesheet="index.css" inside a PackageAssets), those paths must resolve against the package's source_root instead — the package may live in the Typst cache, far outside project_root.

Depends on: rh-A (the previous issue introducing ResolvedPackage and changing the trait signature).

Implementation steps:

1. Read the current resolve_assets in crates/cli/src/lib.rs:416-526 carefully. It iterates plugin.assets() (the AssetConfig declarations) and for each calls plugin_section.get_strings_with_block(asset_config.name) to gather (block, path) pairs.

2. Change the signature of resolve_assets to additionally accept the resolved package blocks:

   fn resolve_assets(
       plugin: &dyn FormatPlugin,
       plugin_section: &PluginSection,
       package_blocks: &[PackageAssets],   // NEW
       project_root: &Path,
       plugin_output_dir: &Path,
   ) -> Result<HashMap<&'static str, Vec<Asset>>>

3. For each AssetConfig the plugin declares, in addition to gathering pairs from plugin_section.asset_blocks() (existing logic), also gather from each PackageAssets.assets.extra. For package-derived pairs, the resolution root is package.source_root, not project_root. Track per-pair resolution roots so the existing grouping by dest still works but each path is joined to its correct root.

   Track also whether each pair originated from a package block. Suggested shape:

       Vec<(Option<&str> dest, &Path resolution_root, &str path, bool is_package_default)>

   Group by (dest, resolution_root). When checking abs.is_file() at line 458, use resolution_root.join(path) instead of project_root.join(path). When passing to copy_each at line 480, pass the per-group resolution_root in place of project_root.

4. SUPPRESS the "asset override path not found, skipping" warning at crates/cli/src/lib.rs:471 when is_package_default is true. Reason: package-injected defaults (like index.css from rh-C) are conventional, not user-requested — most packages won't have them and we should not noisily warn for every such package. The warning must still fire for missing user-listed override paths.

5. Grouping rationale (do NOT collapse): collisions are detected via seen_relative_paths keyed on the *output* relative path (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:490), which is root-agnostic. Cross-root output-name collisions still fail loudly even though groups are split by resolution_root. Do not "fix" this by collapsing groups — the per-group copy_each call needs a single source root.

6. Update the call site at crates/cli/src/lib.rs:562 to pass package_blocks. The package_blocks variable is computed later (line 601) — move the resolve_packages + map_packages_to_assets calls above resolve_assets so package_blocks is in scope.

7. The bulk-copy loop at crates/cli/src/lib.rs:608-644 (which copies the package's **/* into plugin_output_dir/<dest>/) stays unchanged. Both passes are independent: the bulk copy handles user-data files; resolve_assets handles named-asset injection.

8. Add unit tests in crates/cli/src/lib.rs alongside the existing resolve_assets tests (line 1192 onward):

   a) test_resolve_assets_package_block_css_override: build a temp dir with pkg/index.css, construct a PackageAssets { source_root: <pkg>, assets: PluginAssets { copy: vec![], dest: Some("pkg"), extra: { "css_stylesheet": "index.css" } } }, call resolve_assets with empty plugin_section asset_blocks, assert resolved.get("css_stylesheet").unwrap()[0].built_relative_path == "pkg/index.css".

   b) test_resolve_assets_package_block_optional_missing_skips: same as above but no index.css on disk; resolve_assets returns Ok with no css_stylesheet entry; AND assert no warning was logged for the package default (use tracing-test or capture stderr — match whatever convention existing tests use, otherwise leave the no-warning aspect as a manual check noted in a comment).

   c) test_resolve_assets_user_block_still_uses_project_root: verify the existing user-block path resolves against project_root unchanged when package_blocks is empty (regression guard).

   d) test_resolve_assets_user_and_package_collision: user block has [[html.assets]] dest="pkg" css_stylesheet="x.css" with project_root/x.css existing, and a package block has source_root/<pkg>/x.css with css_stylesheet="x.css" dest="pkg". Both groups produce output "pkg/x.css" — assert resolve_assets returns an Err matching the existing "asset path collision" message. Verifies the new grouping does not bypass seen_relative_paths.

9. Run: cargo build && cargo fmt && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo test.

Acceptance: resolve_assets accepts package_blocks; css/js overrides on a PackageAssets are resolved relative to that block's source_root and copied into plugin_output_dir/<dest>/; missing package-default paths do not emit warnings; existing tests still pass; new tests pass.

title: HTML plugin overrides map_packages_to_assets with index.css/index.js defaults
description:
Background: After rh-A and rh-B, the FormatPlugin::map_packages_to_assets trait method takes &[ResolvedPackage] and returns Vec<PackageAssets>, and resolve_assets resolves overrides on package blocks relative to package.source_root. Now the HTML plugin should override this method to wire conventional defaults: when a package is declared via packages = ["./pkg"] under [html], the package's own index.css and index.js should be picked up as the html plugin's css_stylesheet and js_scripts assets without requiring the user to repeat them in [[html.assets]].

Depends on: rh-A, rh-B.

Implementation steps:

1. Open crates/html/src/lib.rs. The plugin currently relies on the default map_packages_to_assets. Add an explicit override on the impl FormatPlugin block.

2. Implementation — reuse the default_package_assets helper from rh-A so we don't duplicate the copy/dest construction:

   fn map_packages_to_assets(&self, packages: &[ResolvedPackage]) -> Vec<PackageAssets> {
       packages
           .iter()
           .map(|pkg| {
               let mut block = default_package_assets(pkg);
               block.assets.extra.insert(
                   "css_stylesheet".into(),
                   toml::Value::String("index.css".into()),
               );
               block.assets.extra.insert(
                   "js_scripts".into(),
                   toml::Value::String("index.js".into()),
               );
               block
           })
           .collect()
   }

   Add the necessary imports (ResolvedPackage, default_package_assets) from rheo_core::plugins — match whichever paths the html crate already uses for FormatPlugin and AssetConfig.

3. User-override interaction (DECISION REQUIRED — implement as STACKING):

   If a user already declares [[html.assets]] dest = "<pkgname>" css_stylesheet = "custom.css", the synthetic package block contributes a *second* css_stylesheet entry. Both flow through get_strings_with_block (crates/core/src/config.rs:306-311) and both get injected into <head>. This is consistent with resolve_assets's general multi-block stacking semantics.

   Add a unit test asserting this stacking:
   - Construct a PluginSection with a user [[html.assets]] dest="pkg" css_stylesheet="custom.css" and a package block (via rh-B's path) contributing dest="pkg" css_stylesheet="index.css".
   - Assert resolved.get("css_stylesheet") has BOTH "pkg/custom.css" and "pkg/index.css" in built_relative_path values.

   If at review time the user prefers SUPPRESSION (user block silences the package default), revisit this issue before implementing.

4. Note: index.css and index.js are optional. If a package doesn't have them, resolve_assets in rh-B silently skips them (and per rh-B step 4, does NOT emit a warning for these package defaults). This is the intended behavior.

5. The existing HTML injection logic (html_utils::inject_head_links / script injection) reads from ctx.assets.get("css_stylesheet") and ctx.assets.get("js_scripts") and is unchanged. Resolved package assets flow through the same HashMap and get appended to whatever the user already declared.

6. Run: cargo build && cargo fmt && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo test.

Acceptance: HTML plugin's map_packages_to_assets returns one PackageAssets per ResolvedPackage with extra css_stylesheet/js_scripts defaults via default_package_assets; stacking with user [[html.assets]] for the same dest is asserted by a unit test; integration test in rh-D passes.

title: epub crate mixes anyhow and RheoError inconsistently
description:
The epub crate uses `anyhow::Result` internally for a large portion of EPUB generation — `generate_package`, `zip_epub`, `generate_nav_xhtml`, and the inner closure of `compile_epub_impl` — then converts at the boundary:

    epub/src/lib.rs:310-313
    inner().map_err(|e| RheoError::EpubGeneration {
        count: 1,
        errors: e.to_string(),
    })?;

This is the only crate in the workspace that takes this approach. It:
- Adds `anyhow` as an explicit dependency
- Produces inconsistent error message chains compared to the rest of the codebase
- Makes it harder to provide structured error context (anyhow chains are just strings)

The root cause is likely the many third-party crates (`zip`, `iref`, `anyhow`-using dependencies) whose errors don't implement `Into<RheoError>`.

Fix: Add `From` implementations or use the existing `RheoError::InvalidData` / `RheoError::EpubGeneration` variants with `.map_err()` at each call site. The `zip` and `iref` errors can be converted to `RheoError::EpubGeneration` inline. This eliminates the `anyhow` dependency from the epub crate entirely and makes error handling consistent with `pdf` and `html`.
close_reason: Replaced anyhow::Result with RheoError throughout epub crate

title: get_files_for_plugin loses spine ordering
description:
`cli/src/lib.rs:255-276` filters `project.typ_files` by the spine glob results using a `HashSet`:

    let spine_set: HashSet<_> = spine_files.iter().collect();
    Ok(project.typ_files.iter()
        .filter(|f| spine_set.contains(f))
        .collect())

`project.typ_files` is collected in walk order (unsorted). The spine glob results are sorted by filename within each pattern. Filtering through `HashSet` membership discards the spine's declared order — the resulting per-file compilation visits files in walk order, not the order the user declared in `vertebrae`.

This matters when output files have interdependencies (e.g., a chapter that imports a table of contents built from prior chapters) and when predictable output naming is important.

Fix: Instead of filtering `project.typ_files`, return `spine_files` directly (already in the correct order). When there's no spine config, fall back to `project.typ_files` sorted lexicographically. The filter step is only needed to exclude files not in the spine, which `generate_spine` already handles by only returning matched files.
close_reason: Returns spine files directly instead of filtering through HashSet

title: Convert inject_head_links to HtmlDom method
description:
Move inject_head_links from a standalone function to a method on HtmlDom.

## Background

inject_head_links(html: &str, fonts: &[&str], stylesheets: &[&str], scripts: &[&str]) -> Result<String> in crates/core/src/html_utils.rs lines 263-294 parses HTML into an HtmlDom, creates link/script elements, prepends them to the head, and serializes. This is naturally a method on HtmlDom. inject_inline_styles (lines 232-256) should remain standalone — it operates on raw strings because DOM parsing would mangle CSS selectors.

## Steps

1. In crates/core/src/html_utils.rs, add a new method to impl HtmlDom: pub fn inject_head_links(&mut self, fonts: &[&str], stylesheets: &[&str], scripts: &[&str]) -> Result<()> — move the body of the standalone function, skip HtmlDom::parse (already have self), skip final serialize (caller does that)
2. Keep the standalone inject_head_links function as a thin wrapper: parse html, call method, serialize
3. Run cargo test — test for inject_head_links in html_utils.rs should still pass

## Expected outcome

HtmlDom gains an inject_head_links method. Standalone function preserved as wrapper. inject_inline_styles unchanged.
